videos.title: One Word Can Change What You Remember Seeing
videos.topic: The misinformation effect: a single word in a question can change what people remember seeing, as shown in the classic car-crash memory experiment.
videos.genre: a surprising quirk of how memory works

videos.title: The Hidden Bias That Quietly Steers Your Guesses
videos.topic: Anchoring bias: the first number we hear pulls our later estimates toward it, shown in Tversky and Kahneman's rigged wheel experiment.
videos.genre: a hidden bias that shapes everyday decisions

videos.title: Why You Sing Quieter in a Group (Social Loafing)
videos.topic: Social loafing: people tend to put in less effort when their work is pooled in a group (the Ringelmann rope-pulling effect)
videos.genre: why people behave strangely in groups

videos.title: The Simple If-Then Trick That Beats Procrastination
videos.topic: Implementation intentions: making a specific if-then plan helps people follow through on goals more than a vague intention alone (Peter Gollwitzer's research).
videos.genre: the psychology of habits and procrastination

videos.title: The Gorilla Experiment That Proved You Miss Obvious Things
videos.topic: The invisible gorilla experiment by Simons and Chabris showed inattentional blindness: when attention is locked on a task, many people miss a obvious, unexpected event.
videos.genre: a famous psychology experiment and what it revealed

videos.title: You Judge People Before They Speak. Here's Why
videos.topic: Thin slicing: people form surprisingly quick impressions from silent, seconds-long clips of body language, and Ambady and Rosenthal found these snap ratings of teachers tended to match end-of-semester student ratings.

videos.title: Why Vague Horoscopes Feel Like They're Just for You
videos.topic: The Forer (Barnum) effect: people accept vague, general statements as personal descriptions of themselves, as shown in Bertram Forer's 1948 classroom demonstration.
videos.genre: why the brain falls for certain tricks and illusions

videos.title: Why Everyone Noticed Your Awkward Moment Less Than You Think
videos.topic: The spotlight effect: people overestimate how much others notice their embarrassing moments, shown in Gilovich's embarrassing T-shirt experiment
videos.genre: the science of emotions like boredom, nostalgia or awkwardness

videos.title: You've Seen It 1,000 Times, But Can You Draw It?
videos.topic: Nickerson and Adams found that people see a penny constantly but struggle to draw it or pick the real one from fakes, because memory keeps only what is useful.
videos.genre: a surprising quirk of how memory works

videos.title: Why You Can't Quit Boring Things (Sunk Cost Effect)
videos.topic: The sunk cost effect: we keep doing something because we've already invested time or money in it, even when quitting would be better.
videos.genre: a hidden bias that shapes everyday decisions

videos.title: Why You Nod Along With a Group (Asch's Famous Experiment)
videos.topic: Asch's conformity experiment: people often go along with a group's obviously wrong answer, but a single dissenter makes it easier to speak up.
videos.genre: why people behave strangely in groups

videos.title: Habits Don't Take 21 Days. Here's What Research Found
videos.topic: A University College London study found habits took about 66 days on average to feel automatic, with a huge range between people, so the '21 days' idea is a myth.
videos.genre: the psychology of habits and procrastination

videos.title: Paid $1 to Lie, They Started Believing It
videos.topic: Festinger and Carlsmith's cognitive dissonance experiment: people paid only $1 to say a boring task was fun later rated it as more enjoyable than people paid $20
videos.genre: a famous psychology experiment and what it revealed
